title: Dofollow Backlinks Guide: How to Get Links That Pass Real Authority
content_html:
Not all backlinks are created equal, but some pass authority from one site to another while others do little more than exist. Dofollow backlinks are the type that actually move the needle for search rankings. This guide breaks down what dofollow backlinks are, why they matter, and how to build the kind that move your site up the results page.

Key Takeaway: Dofollow backlinks are the only link type that passes full link equity and authority from the linking page to your site. To earn them at scale, focus on creating link-worthy content, building relationships with authoritative publishers, and targeting niche-relevant domains with genuine value to offer. Quality and relevance matter far more than raw volume.

What Are Dofollow Backlinks?

Dofollow backlinks are standard hyperlinks that allow search engines to follow them and pass link equity from the source page to the destination page. Unlike nofollow links, which carry a rel attribute telling crawlers to ignore the connection, dofollow links have no special attribute attached. They are the default state of any hyperlink on the web.

When a website links to your content with a dofollow link, it is essentially vouching for your page. Google and other search engines interpret that vote of confidence as a signal that your content is trustworthy and relevant. The more high-quality dofollow backlinks your site accumulates, the stronger its overall authority becomes in the eyes of search algorithms.

How Dofollow Links Differ From Nofollow

The difference between dofollow and nofollow links comes down to a single HTML attribute. A nofollow link includes rel="nofollow" in its anchor tag, which instructs search engines not to follow the link or pass authority. A dofollow link has no such attribute, so crawlers follow it by default and transfer equity through it.

This distinction matters because it determines whether a backlink contributes to your search rankings. A nofollow link from a major publication still drives referral traffic and brand awareness, but it does not directly boost your page authority. A dofollow link from the same publication does both, making it significantly more valuable for SEO purposes.

The rel Attribute Explained

The rel attribute defines the relationship between the linking page and the linked page. For dofollow links, no rel attribute is needed because following and passing equity is the default behavior. For links that should not pass equity, webmasters add rel values like nofollow, sponsored, or ugc to modify how search engines treat them.

Google introduced the sponsored and ugc attributes in 2019 to give publishers more granular control. Links marked as sponsored tell crawlers the link is part of a paid arrangement, while links marked as ugc indicate user-generated content like comments or forum posts. Both function similarly to nofollow in that they do not pass full link equity to the destination page.

Why Dofollow Backlinks Matter for SEO

Dofollow backlinks remain one of the top ranking factors in Google's algorithm. They function as third-party endorsements that help search engines determine which pages deserve to rank for a given query. Without a solid backlink profile, even well-optimized content can struggle to reach the first page of search results.

The value of a dofollow link depends on the authority of the linking domain, the relevance of the linking page, and the placement of the link within the content. A single dofollow link from a trusted industry publication can outperform dozens of links from low-quality directories. This is why link building strategy should always prioritize quality over quantity.

Link Equity and PageRank Flow

Link equity, sometimes called link juice, is the authority a page passes through its outbound links. When a high-authority page links to your site with a dofollow link, a portion of that authority flows to your page. The amount of equity transferred depends on the linking page's total authority and how many other outbound links it contains.

Pages with fewer outbound links pass more equity per link. This is why a link from a niche blog with few outbound connections can sometimes deliver more value than a link from a major site that links out hundreds of times. Understanding this dynamic helps you prioritize link opportunities that offer the highest potential return.

Authority Transfer Signals

Google evaluates multiple signals when determining how much authority a dofollow link transfers. Domain reputation, page-level relevance, and the contextual placement of the link all play a role. Links embedded naturally within editorial content carry more weight than links stuffed into footers or sidebars.

Anchor text also provides context about the linked page's topic. Using descriptive anchor text that aligns with your target keywords helps search engines understand what your page is about. However, over-optimizing anchor text with exact-match keywords can trigger spam filters, so variety and natural phrasing are essential.

How to Identify Dofollow Backlinks

Before you can evaluate your backlink profile, you need to know which links are dofollow and which are not. Identifying link types requires inspecting the HTML of the linking page or using specialized SEO tools that surface this information automatically. Both approaches have their place in a comprehensive link audit.

Manual Inspection Methods

The most direct way to check a link type is to view the page source and locate the anchor tag. Right-click on the linking page, select view source, and search for the URL of your site. If the anchor tag contains rel="nofollow", rel="sponsored", or rel="ugc", the link is not dofollow.

Browser extensions can speed up this process significantly. Tools like the NoFollow extension for Chrome and Firefox highlight nofollow links directly on the page with a dotted red underline. This visual approach lets you scan an entire page quickly without digging through source code for every link.

Tools for Backlink Analysis

SEO platforms like Ahrefs, Semrush, and Moz provide detailed backlink reports that classify each link as dofollow or nofollow. These tools aggregate data across your entire backlink profile, making it easy to see the ratio of dofollow to nofollow links and identify patterns over time. For a deeper look at link building strategy, explore our link building services.

Google Search Console also offers insight into your backlink profile through its Links report. While it does not explicitly label links as dofollow or nofollow, it shows top linking sites and pages, which you can then inspect manually. Combining Search Console data with a dedicated backlink tool gives you the most complete picture.

Strategies to Build High-Quality Dofollow Backlinks

Earning dofollow backlinks requires a deliberate approach. The strategies that worked a decade ago, like submitting to thousands of directories or buying links, no longer produce results and can trigger penalties. Today, the most effective link building methods focus on creating genuine value that authoritative sites want to reference.

Content-Driven Link Building

Creating original research, data studies, and comprehensive guides is one of the most reliable ways to attract dofollow backlinks naturally. Journalists and bloggers constantly search for credible data to support their articles, and they typically link to the source with a dofollow link. If your content provides unique insights, it becomes a citation asset.

Infographics and visual assets also earn links at high rates because they are easy to embed and reference. When you publish an infographic, include an embed code that uses a dofollow link back to your site. This makes it effortless for other publishers to share your visual while passing authority to your domain.

Digital PR and Outreach

Digital PR involves pitching your content, expertise, or data to journalists and publishers who cover your industry. When a journalist references your contribution in an article, the resulting link is typically dofollow. This approach combines link building with brand visibility, delivering value beyond SEO alone.

Successful outreach requires personalization and relevance. Generic email templates get ignored, but targeted pitches that demonstrate genuine familiarity with the recipient's work earn responses. Start by building a list of publications and writers in your niche, then craft pitches that offer something their audience cannot find elsewhere.

Guest Posting on Authority Sites

Guest posting remains one of the most controllable ways to earn dofollow backlinks. When you contribute a high-quality article to an authoritative site in your industry, you typically receive at least one dofollow link in your author bio or within the content body. The key is targeting sites with real editorial standards rather than those that accept any submission.

Avoid sites that exist solely to publish guest posts, as these are often flagged as link farms and provide little to no SEO value. Focus on established publications with engaged audiences where your content can drive both authority and referral traffic. For a broader approach to improving your search visibility, consider our search engine optimization services.

Broken Link Building

Broken link building involves finding dead links on authoritative sites and offering your content as a replacement. When a webmaster updates a broken link to point to your page, the resulting link is almost always dofollow. This strategy works because it helps the linking site fix a problem while giving you a valuable backlink.

To execute this strategy, use a crawler tool to scan target sites for broken outbound links. Identify links that pointed to content similar to what you have published, then reach out to the site owner with a polite message explaining the broken link and suggesting your page as an alternative. Keep the message concise and focused on helping them, not asking for a favor.

Dofollow vs Nofollow vs Sponsored Links

Understanding the differences between link types helps you evaluate your backlink profile and plan your link building efforts. Each type serves a different purpose and sends a different signal to search engines. The table below compares the three primary link types.

When Each Link Type Is Appropriate

Dofollow links are appropriate when a site genuinely endorses your content without any financial arrangement. Nofollow links are suitable for situations where the site owner does not want to vouch for the linked content, such as user comments or links to untrusted sources. Sponsored links should be used whenever a financial relationship exists between the linker and the linked site.

A healthy backlink profile contains a mix of all three types. A profile with only dofollow links can look unnatural to search engines, but including some nofollow and sponsored links signals that your link acquisition is organic rather than manipulated. Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many site owners undermine their link building efforts by making avoidable mistakes. These errors can waste time, squander link equity, or even trigger search penalties. Recognizing these pitfalls early helps you build a backlink profile that delivers long-term results.

Low-Quality Directory Links

Submitting your site to every free directory you can find is a strategy that stopped working years ago. Most low-quality directories carry no authority and exist only to collect submissions. Links from these sources add no value to your profile and can even harm your rankings if Google identifies them as part of a link scheme.

Instead, focus on a small number of high-quality, niche-specific directories. Industry associations, local business directories, and curated resource lists can still provide valuable dofollow links. Evaluate each directory by checking its own backlink profile and domain authority before submitting your site.

Over-Optimized Anchor Text

Using the same exact-match anchor text for every backlink is a red flag for search engines. Google's algorithms look for natural variation in anchor text across a backlink profile. If every link to your site uses the same keyword phrase, it signals manipulation rather than organic linking.

Aim for a diverse anchor text distribution that includes branded terms, partial match phrases, generic terms like "click here," and natural variations of your target keywords. A healthy profile might have 40 to 50 percent branded anchors, 20 to 30 percent partial match, and the remainder split among exact match and generic terms.

Ignoring Relevance

A dofollow link from a site unrelated to your niche passes far less value than one from a topically relevant source. Google uses topical relevance to determine how much weight a link should carry. A link from a cooking blog to a software company does not provide the same signal as a link from a technology publication.

Prioritize link opportunities from sites that cover topics related to your industry. This ensures the authority transferred through the link is contextually meaningful. Relevant links also tend to drive more referral traffic, adding a secondary benefit beyond the SEO value.

Measuring the Impact of Your Dofollow Backlinks

Building dofollow backlinks is only half the equation. You also need to measure their impact on your search performance to understand which efforts are paying off. Tracking the right metrics helps you refine your strategy and allocate resources toward the most effective tactics.

Key Metrics to Track

Start by monitoring your total number of referring domains, not just total backlinks. Multiple links from the same domain carry diminishing returns, so the number of unique linking domains is a stronger indicator of progress. Track this metric over time to see whether your link building efforts are expanding your reach.

Also track keyword rankings for pages receiving new dofollow links. If rankings improve after a link is acquired, that connection validates the value of the link. Monitor organic traffic growth to pages with active link building campaigns to measure the cumulative effect of your backlink acquisition.

Tools for Monitoring Backlink Performance

Ahrefs and Semrush both offer backlink monitoring features that track new and lost links over time. Set up alerts so you receive notifications when your site gains or loses a referring domain. This allows you to respond quickly to lost links, perhaps by reaching out to the site owner to understand what happened.

Google Search Console provides a free baseline for monitoring your link profile. While it lacks the detailed metrics of paid tools, it shows linking sites, top linked pages, and anchor text data. Combine it with a paid tool for a comprehensive monitoring setup that covers both quantity and quality signals.

Building a Sustainable Dofollow Backlink Strategy

Sustainable link building is about systems, not shortcuts. The sites that consistently earn high-quality dofollow backlinks do so by creating valuable content, building real relationships, and maintaining high editorial standards. Short-term tactics like buying links or participating in link exchanges may produce temporary gains but carry long-term risks.

Start by auditing your existing content to identify link-worthy assets. Look for pages with original data, comprehensive guides, or unique tools that other sites would naturally reference. If you do not have these assets yet, prioritize creating them before investing heavily in outreach.

Develop a repeatable outreach process that includes prospecting, personalized pitching, and follow-up. Track your outreach in a spreadsheet or CRM so you can measure response rates and refine your approach over time. The most successful link builders treat outreach as an ongoing practice rather than a one-time campaign.

Finally, remember that dofollow backlinks are a means to an end, not the end itself. The goal is to build authority that drives organic traffic and generates business results. A link from a relevant, authoritative site that sends qualified referral traffic is worth more than a dozen links from sites no one visits, so if you need help building a link strategy tailored to your business, reach out to our team to get started.

Dofollow backlinks remain a cornerstone of search engine optimization. By understanding how they work, avoiding common mistakes, and committing to sustainable acquisition methods, you can build a backlink profile that strengthens your site's authority for years to come. The effort required is significant, but the compounding returns make it one of the highest-ROI activities in digital marketing.
